findings.reason: The route's assertion that the general Eisenstein inputs are unplanned conflicts with AS.1, AS.2, AS.4 and AF.3, read against §§4.2–4.3, pp. 34–39, and the accepted BP–Chaudouard–Zydor /28 and Jiang–Zhang route 3. Import cuspidal convergence, constant terms, continuation, and rapid decay. Split off residual inducing data and the particular MW normalization, cone, pole-detection and Hermitian-symmetry results; the existing contracts do not automatically supply every one of these extensions. Request them from their spectral owner before treating them as planned.

The brief both imports and rebuilds Langlands quotients. Gan–Savin route 3 assigns the general p-adic classification to SR.3; Chenevier–Taïbi, Gan–Ichino and Nelson–Venkatesh assign the archimedean inputs to AF.1. Sections 3.1, 3.4 and 3.6 use both regimes. Split the classification, archimedean GL_n correspondence, and classical-group parameter/central/infinitesimal compatibility. AF.1b is a proposed successor in RT-AREA-automorphic-1.fixes.md, absent from the assembled atlas at this review's base, so it must be referenced conditionally. Preserve the doubling-specific realizations.

Appendix A, pp. 43–55, invokes general Dixmier–Malliavin, classification, unitary generic exponent bounds and Jacquet–Shalika inputs. Accepted Jiang–Zhang routes 5–6, BP–Chaudouard–Zydor routes 6–7, and Gan–Ichino route 6 already assign these to ET.6, AF.1 and AL.3. Coalesce those sources, including the conflicting Jacquet–Shalika owner proposals. Split bundled items: the specific holomorphy application and holomorphic-family factorization are not supplied simply by importing their general foundations.

The rs-factors item marks the entire generic and non-generic statement planned at AL.3. Its current contract supplies generic Whittaker theory and cuspidal unfolding, not arbitrary Langlands-data factors; the AL packet does not establish that missing extension. The uses in §3.4, p. 17, and Appendix A must distinguish generic factors from products for non-generic Langlands quotients. Retain the former as planned and request the latter from AL.3 with SR.3/AF.1 inputs, rather than creating a second factor owner.

The item combines standard GL_n factors, Rankin–Selberg pole/absolute-convergence results and boundary nonvanishing, but credits all of them to AL.3. AL.2 owns the standard factors, and accepted BP–Chaudouard–Zydor /70 still requests the boundary theorem. Moreover E11 and p. 36 give M_2=(L(2s)/L(2s+c′))N_2: the corrected argument needs numerator holomorphy on Re(2s)≥1 and denominator nonvanishing on Re(2s+c′)≥2. Split ownership and retain a missing boundary input only where actually used.

The ET.7a attribution bundles residual Speh construction with the nonzero global (k,c) coefficient and its factorization used in the unfolding on p. 39. Split those exports; the latter is not supplied by ET.7a's classification statement. Its present requires list has four entries, and I independently counted 437 ancestors, including AS.6 and ET.4; the report's older count of 239 is obsolete. Request an early residual supplier independent of trace comparison, without modifying upstream or declaring an untested new dependency cycle.

For tempered p-adic τ, the descending-twist quotient defining ρ_c(τ) agrees with the ascending-twist subrepresentation in accepted Atobe–Kondo–Yasuda /speh, source-routed to ET.6. Thus the constructor overlap is real. The remedy must be narrower than marking every field and generic τ planned: unitary non-tempered data, archimedean construction, and the (k,c) model/wavefront/multiplicity results still require separate plans or owner requests. Merge the specialized integral/model work into the shared Part II.

The pinned Tau Ceti ConstantForm Basic groupScheme and mem_definingPointsSubgroup_iff already supply the quotient enforcing M C Mᵀ=C; Symplectic Basic specializes it to J, and Mathlib supplies Matrix.symplecticGroup. SpecialLinear supplies the determinant-one cut. These are partial reusable foundations, not all of groups. Explicitly reconcile the form orientation with CFK's MᵀJM=J. SpecialOrthogonal Basic uses C=1 and cannot silently be identified with split SO_J. Import upstream ReductiveGroups layers 7–8 and RG.2.5; retain GSpin, the similitude character, embeddings and other missing constructions.

Theorem 0.1 and Definitions 2.1–2.2, pp. 2 and 8–9, require a number field, c>1, the type-dependent target rank, irreducible cuspidal data, and the archimedean infinitesimal-character condition in weak transfer. Theorem 4.10, p. 41, quantifies all generic twists and all k. Restore those scopes. Remark 4.9 concerns the particular constructed transfer's archimedean component; it does not upgrade every weak transfer to that stronger conclusion.

The result has no top-level prerequisites list although its statements and §§2–4 repeatedly use CFK22, CFGK23 and GK23 for the construction, local functional equation, models and multiplicity one. These are structural dependencies, not incidental bibliography; their references were checked on pp. 55–57. Add explicit source prerequisites and accessible-source/owner dispositions for the further main-chain inputs. Reconcile these with already routed mathematics instead of reproducing the red team's historical atlas counts or making each reference a new roadmap.

The standing characteristic-zero setting on p. 6 and the explicit local scope on p. 42 are not carried by many local item statements. A shared informal note cannot license positive-characteristic versions of the constructions, factors or stability theorem. Add the field and representation hypotheses to each affected statement or an explicit inherited scope, including archimedean versus nonarchimedean cases. This confirms an extraction defect, not failure of a positive-characteristic theorem actually stated by CFK.

The proofs of Lemmas 3.13–3.14, pp. 19–20, cite support, asymptotic and Schwartz estimates from JPSS79a, Jac09, JR96, AGJ09 and FJ93, and use CFGK23 equivariance and DM factorization. The listed prerequisites do not cover these steps. Add the precise (k,c)-model adaptations and dependencies, importing general Whittaker and smooth-representation estimates from their owners. The primary paper's citation establishes the proof obligation; it does not independently verify the cited general theorem or an adaptation beyond its original scope.

Proposition 3.17, p. 24, and the Appendix convergence arguments require matrix-coefficient growth bounds for the GL_l inducing representation. Z2's dependencies do not include the cited nonarchimedean central-exponent estimates or the archimedean polynomial bound with representation-dependent exponent. Add these inputs and their application. Coordinate general growth estimates with SR.3 and AF.1, whose moderate-growth foundations already overlap, rather than rebuilding an unrestricted archimedean growth theory in the doubling Part II.

Proposition 3.18 and Lemma 3.20, pp. 27–31, explicitly use HS16's GSpin projection calculation, Yamana's open-cell result and Soudry's Iwasawa bounds. None is a separately stated prerequisite. Add the projections and geometric estimates with the precise group adaptations; the SO result alone does not prove the claimed Sp/GSpin analogues. Preserve the statement of the open embedding and explain the adaptation, instead of treating “similar bounds” as a checked theorem.

Corollary 3.21's proof on p. 32 needs a finite convolution decomposition whose resulting sections remain entire in s, citing Gourevitch's CFK22 Appendix A. The extracted DM item asserts only factorization for a fixed smooth representation. Add the holomorphic-family theorem and meromorphic-section framework, importing the classical AF.1 factorization. Its actual family hypotheses and continuity must be checked in that appendix; this review confirms the omitted obligation, not the complete external family proof.

The first part of rev-bounds-for-smooth-matrix-coefficients-of is Sun's continuous-seminorm bound by Ξ on p. 33. Accepted Nelson–Venkatesh /40 already routes the corresponding Sobolev-bound interface to QuantitativeOrbitMethodAndSpectralAsymptotics. Record one shared supplier and the seminorm/Sobolev comparison needed by CFK. Retain the separate Wallach convergence application locally; overlap in this bound does not justify importing all orbit-method estimates or crediting every term of the bundled item as planned.

Theorem 3.12, p. 19, covers k=1, but poles-local has no prerequisite edge to the extracted Yamana adaptation. CFK explicitly separates that case from the k>1 reduction and calls for adjustments to the groups. Add the existing k=1 item as an edge and describe the O-to-SO/GSpin adaptation as work to prove. The converse twisting set includes characters, so restricting the brief to Appendix A's k>1 argument leaves a main-chain gap.

Page 40 asserts right-half-plane absolute convergence of the partial standard Euler product. AL.4's contract makes convergence conditional on a supplied eigenvalue bound; the extraction supplies no such bound. Add a uniform unramified unitary Satake-growth estimate and the Euler-product argument, with the standard representation and Haar/Frobenius conventions. Naming a possible root-theoretic or spherical-unitary argument is a proof plan, not evidence that the required bound is already an atlas export.

The unitary reduction at the start of §4.4, p. 40, is absent from main/coarse-global's graph. For GSpin the missing steps are π=|Υ_c|^s π_0 globally and compatibility of transfer with |det|^s at unramified and infinite places. From the datum on pp. 6–7, Υ_c=2e_0+Σe_i pairs to 1 with each standard dual weight, while the central character twists by |·|^{2s}. Record the global unitarization proof and twist compatibilities before extending the unitary construction to every cuspidal π.

The stated all-partial-sums criterion is false for k=1 in type D. Using the simple roots on pp. 6–7, the two terminal fundamental coweights require both Σ_{i<c}Re(e_i)−Re(e_c)<0 and Σ_{i≤c}Re(e_i)<0, besides the shorter prefixes. For c=2, (−0.1,−5) satisfies the printed partial sums but violates the first terminal inequality. Restrict the type-C formula and prove the type-D k=1 case separately. This counterexample concerns the extracted criterion, not CFK's final holomorphy theorem.

Page 41 explicitly uses global genericity of cuspidal GL_l data and the genericity of their local components; §§4.3–4.4 require it for every local twisting representation as well. No extracted item supplies this. Accepted Yu /127 assigns the Fourier/Whittaker interface to AL.3, so add that input and the local-factorization consequence, coordinating any required global-prefix extension with AL.3. AF.3's cuspidality alone is insufficient; an accepted paper attribution does not mean this analytic construction is formalized.

Page 50 cites Bernstein's continuation principle through Ban98 for general nonarchimedean π. I independently read the reproduced theorem in Banks, pp. 782–783: countable-dimensional V, an irreducible algebraic parameter variety, regular linear equations, and uniqueness on a nonempty ordinary open set yield a rational solution generically outside countably many hypersurfaces. State those hypotheses and the normalized-functional application as a missing input. Distinguish this theorem from Banks's additional holomorphy/pole corollary and from CFK's narrower multiplicativity continuation.

The extraction repeats the inconsistent source notation; p. 12 also uses it in the dual Levi map. Correct the lattice types and record the source discrepancy rather than silently changing the paper. This check is against arXiv v5 and makes no claim about a correction in the inaccessible journal text.
